title: Ordex overview
summary: The workspace header: home, detail level, search and the network and gateway settings, then the goals on the Launchpad.

steps.title: Home
steps.content: The Ordex mark always returns to the Launchpad, where every task starts.

steps.title: Level of detail
steps.content: Choose Plain English for outcomes, Builder for API fields, or Protocol Proof for the exact verifier rules.

steps.title: Search and jump
steps.content: Press Ctrl+K or / to find a mission, an API operation or a refusal code and go straight to it.

steps.title: Network and gateway
steps.content: Settings hold the network (mainnet by default), an optional gateway origin and read-only or write mode. Tools label every result with them.

steps.title: Start from a goal
steps.content: Pick what you want to do; the Launchpad suggests the missions that get you there.

title: Publish and settle public asks
summary: Follow the public ask mission, see what evidence completes a stage, then replay a purchase in the Sandbox.

steps.title: Eight stages
steps.content: A mission moves from Understand to Finish. A stage completes only when a tool records matching evidence, never from a click.

steps.title: What completes a stage
steps.content: Each stage names the tool run that counts as evidence and links to that tool.

steps.title: Replay the purchase
steps.content: Play the scenario step by step. Every verdict comes from the reference verifier running in your browser.

title: Inspect what a wallet changed
summary: Paste a PSBT or transaction, read it field by field, and compare it with what came back from a wallet.

steps.title: Paste an artifact
steps.content: Paste a PSBT (hex or Base64) or a raw transaction. It is decoded strictly, in your browser.

steps.title: Views and comparison
steps.content: Read the summary, the structure and the bytes, or compare two artifacts to see every change and how much it matters.
steps.hint: The views appear once an artifact is decoded.

title: Diagnose a refusal
summary: Paste a refusal code or error, read where the verifier refuses and why, and reproduce it.

steps.title: Paste the failure
steps.content: A refusal code, a verifier result, a gateway error, a Doctor report or an event.

steps.title: Reproduce it
steps.content: Every refusal has a checked-in reproducer. Run it here or download a script that runs the reference verifier.
steps.hint: This part appears once a code is diagnosed.

title: Connect an AI coding agent
summary: Build the MCP stdio server, add it to your client, check an HTTP endpoint and try the tools.

steps.title: Build the stdio server
steps.content: One self-contained file, built at the exact revision of this page, with a command to check the install.

steps.title: Add it to your client
steps.content: Setup for Claude Code, Cursor and Codex, with what each client documents about MCP 2026-07-28.

steps.title: Check an HTTP endpoint
steps.content: Real requests from your browser to a docs service: discover, list and one tool call.

steps.title: Try the tools
steps.content: Run any of the ten read-only tools locally in this page, or send the same call to the endpoint.
